transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... most days I just feel like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole. Even when I’m around people I know, I just can't seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.
Have you ever had periods of time where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or impulsive, to the point where it was different from your usual self?

No, not at all. I can't really remember ever feeling like that. Honestly, I don't get bursts of energy or talk a lot... it's pretty much always just the opposite. I've never really been impulsive, either.
Could you tell me how long you have been feeling this way, and have you had any periods of feeling like your normal self during that time?

It's been going on for... about a year and two months now. It started right after I took a fall at my HVAC job. That left me with a back injury, and... well, everything just started unraveling from there. 

And to answer your other question, no, I haven't really had any periods where I felt like my normal self again. It's just been like this the whole time.
During these past fourteen months, have you struggled with poor appetite or overeating, or have you had significant trouble with your sleep?

Well, my eating is just... all over the place. I’ll go most of the day just drinking coffee, really, because the thought of food just turns my stomach. But then late at night, I end up just picking at whatever’s in the cabinet. I'm not even really tasting it, just eating it.
Do you often find yourself feeling down on yourself or like you aren't good enough?

Yeah. Pretty much constantly. I just keep telling myself that I’m useless now, mostly because I can’t work like I used to. I sit around and... well, I just replay every apprentice I let down, and I think about every unpaid bill piling up. It just feels like it proves that I ruined everything.
Do you often feel physically exhausted or like you have very little energy to get through the day?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel physically exhausted. I mean, I'm not doing a whole lot during the day anyway since the injury, so I'm not really burning much energy. It's more just... sitting around, feeling stuck, rather than actually being too tired to move.
Do you find that your mind often wanders or that you have a hard time making simple decisions?

Yeah, definitely. Things like paperwork and old repair diagrams that used to be second nature to me... now they just kind of blur together when I look at them. I’ll just sit there, completely unable to decide something stupid, like which form to even open first.
Are there any hobbies or activities that you used to enjoy that you still find yourself wanting to do now?

Not really. I mean, I used to love doing a lot of things—hiking, painting, going down to the makerspace to tinker with things. I even used to get a real kick out of figuring out a tricky install. 

But now... I don't know, I just don't have the desire to do any of it. I'll just sit there and stare at my supplies, or I'll ignore calls from people trying to get me to go out or work on a project. It just... none of it even feels worth starting anymore.
Given how heavy things have been feeling for you, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living?

Yeah... I have. I've been having these thoughts that everyone would just be better off if I didn't wake up tomorrow. And sometimes... especially when my back is really hurting and I start thinking about all the money worries piling up since I haven't been working... I catch myself actually thinking about ending it. It scares me when my mind goes there, but... yeah, the thoughts are there.
Looking back further than these past fourteen months, have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt this same way before?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt stressed or down, but nothing like this. Never for weeks at a time where everything just felt this... impossible. This is the first time it's ever been this bad.
